about: Birr Castle Demesne candidates from Heritage Trees of Ireland (2009 survey; coordinates converted from Irish Grid, about 100 m and possibly skewed: the register's point for the box hedge is ~500 m from the Formal Gardens). Delivered in data/research/birrcountryireland-verified.json: bir_001 Carroll Oak, bir_002 box hedges, bir_003 dawn redwood. Only three; the 4-tree floor for a place page is not met.

leads.source: Heritage Trees of Ireland, Tree Council of Ireland / Aubrey Fennell (NBDC dataset 27, CC BY 4.0), survey 2009
leads.reason: Hollowing, band 150-200; register only, no second source, no life evidence, no reason beyond age

leads.source: Heritage Trees of Ireland, Tree Council of Ireland / Aubrey Fennell (NBDC dataset 27, CC BY 4.0), survey 2009
leads.reason: Cultivar with banded foliage, band 50-100; register only, nothing about it on the estate pages found, no life evidence

leads.name: Giant redwoods and coast redwoods (nine, about 1860s)
leads.source: https://www.irishtimes.com/life-and-style/people/the-world-s-largest-california-redwood-grove-in-birr-1.2844039 (29 Oct 2016: nine redwoods across the demesne, probably planted around the 1860s; coast redwood by the wettest spot has the greatest girth); birrcastle.com says a coast redwood stands on the lower terrace of the Formal Gardens
leads.reason: No coordinates or measurements; a good depth lead (ask estate or the Tree Register of Ireland for champion figures); the Giants' Grove saplings (planted from 2017 with Crann) are young and not a veteran

leads.name: Himalayan juniper (champion)
leads.source: https://birrcastle.com/?p=5219 (River Garden, described as a champion tree)
leads.reason: No coordinates, no measurements, species not given to the level of a Latin name

leads.name: Carrierea calycina (champion)
leads.source: https://www.irishtimes.com/news/in-birr-s-botanic-wonderland-1.448457 (28 May 2005, grown from Chinese seed, first flowered 2004)
leads.reason: Rare, but no location or measurements; a plant-collector tree rather than a veteran

leads.name: Magnolia delavayi, Castle Terraces (planted about 1912)
leads.source: https://birrcastle.com/?p=5219 (planted by the 5th Earl of Rosse)
leads.reason: Shrubby evergreen, no coordinates; planting date from the owner, but nothing makes it a destination alone

blocked.name: Birr Castle Grey Poplar
blocked.reason: FELLED: blew down in the storm of mid-February 2014 while Ireland's entry in European Tree of the Year; 42 m, about 200 years, the tallest of its kind in the British Isles; the fallen trunk is to be left in place and carved into a river bench (Irish Times, 15 Feb 2014, irishtimes.com/news/environment/european-tree-of-the-year-contender-blows-over-in-storms-1.1692428; also Wikipedia Birr Castle). Register record 430 (2009) predates the fall. Never ship the standing tree; a bench from the trunk is not a tree.
